newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation still up for merger.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation still up for merger.

text.p: Speculation that the proposed merger between office superstores Office Depot Inc and Staples Inc would be completed remained high Tuesday after the U.S. Federal Trade Commission weighed in against the deal on Monday, options traders said.
But some investors did decide to either take profits or cut losses by exiting positions.
"There was a lot of unwinding and there was a lot of new speculation," Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners, said, referring to Office Depot options.
In afternoon trade, Office Depot shares were up 1-7/8 at 19 after slumping 5-1/2 Monday when the FTC voted against the $4 billion combination, arguing it would lead to higher prices for customers.
Staples, which rose nearly two points Monday before the FTC announcement, finished down 1-3/8 and was unchanged at 23-1/4 Tuesday afternoon.
Both stocks were very active.
Frank McGarvey of TFM Investment Group in Philadelphia, said Staples options investors were largely moving out of the March series into April.
"The only thing going on is that people have pretty much given up on March," he said. March options expire at the end of next week.
"You've got people rolling out of March into April," McGarvey added. "People are looking to buy some time."
April options expire on April 19.
The two most active Staples calls were the March 20 and April 22-1/2, with volume of about 1,540 and 2,220 contracts, respectively.
On the put side, the March 22-1/2 traded about 7,875 contracts and the April 20 traded 7,865.
The Staples April 25 put traded 2,860 contracts.
Schwarz said some Office Depot options investors were using the stock's price action and news developments to take profits or undo hedges and others were establishing new positions.
The most active Office Depot option was the April 20 call, with turnover of about 5,065 contracts. The March 20 call traded more than 3,300, the April 17-1/2 about 1,800 and the July 20 about 1,580.
The Office Depot April 17-1/2 put traded 3,115 contracts, making it the most active put of the group.
Schwarz added that volatility in Office Depot options had risen as high as 130 on merger speculation.
"Yesterday was the first day after things fell apart that we saw a decline in volatility," he said. "That decline has evened out here.
"It's still high but it's more manageable around the 90 level."

On Tuesday, OfficeMax Inc had resumed talks to acquire dozens of stores from Staples that could eventually lead to government approval of the Staples/Office Depot merger, sources close to the talks told Reuters. ((--G.Crawford 3124088750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
